rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda concern private relief payments arising from a serviceman's fatal shooting by a sentry, recount existing death or survivorship benefits, characterize the general benefits system as the proper remedy regardless of the precise cause of a service-connected death, and reject special compensation because it would produce inequity. The close factual architecture, reasoning sequence, and repeated language concerning systems of benefits make the relationship substantially stronger than generic veto boilerplate. C02 and C13 contain related arguments about protecting comprehensive, uniform benefit structures from special additions, but neither matches the child's factual and structural pattern as closely as C04.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Federal Government has provided a costly, comprehensive and orderly system of benefits for survivors of members of the Armed Forces who die in service.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Laws administered by the Veterans' Administration and other Federal agencies provide systems of benefits for certain dependent survivors of members of the Armed Forces killed in line of duty.
shared_material.explanation: Both identify an established federal survivorship-benefits system as the central reason to deny an additional private award.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As long as the death is service-connected, these benefits are payable regardless of the cause, whether it be in combat or as the result of a tragic incident like the present one.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Benefits so authorized are generous and are payable to the specified survivors regardless of whether death results from the negligence or wilful misconduct of fellow servicemen or any other person.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive parallel formulation: ordinary benefits apply regardless of the particular cause or fault behind the serviceman's death.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On the night of July 4, 1954, the decedent...was a member of a motorized patrol...The sentry ordered the vehicle to halt and then fired, fatally wounding the decedent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: He failed to obey the sentry's three shouted commands to halt. The sentry then aimed his shotgun at the decedent's legs and fired...and [he] was instantly killed.
shared_material.explanation: Both memoranda narrate a serviceman's fatal shooting by a military sentry after a command or challenge was not obeyed, then evaluate a private relief payment to survivors.

shared_material.child_excerpt: To make such an award in this case would establish a most undesirable precedent...To follow such a course would...jeopardize the entire structure of benefits which has been built up for the protection of servicemen's survivors.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I think it only fair and reasonable to consider the generous, uniform, and assured protection which these systems afford as the exclusive remedy...Any other view would be productive of anomalies and serious inequities.
shared_material.explanation: Both move from the general benefits scheme to a systemic objection against supplemental case-specific relief.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am constrained, therefore, to withhold my approval from H. R. 1315.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accordingly, while regretting the tragic death of the decedent, I am constrained to withhold my approval from S. 820.
shared_material.explanation: The conclusions use closely parallel language, though this closing formula alone would be boilerplate; it reinforces the much more substantive parallels above.
